title: Clothing & Appearance
description: Learn to describe what people are wearing, talk about physical appearance, express size and age, and identify clothing items and accessories in Spanish.

grammar.title: Ser + Adjetivo - Describing Permanent Characteristics
grammar.content:
The verb SER is used to describe inherent, permanent characteristics of people and things. With appearance, we use 'ser' + adjective.

Conjugation of SER:
Yo soy = I am
Tú eres = You are (informal)
Él/Ella/Usted es = He/She/You(formal) is
Nosotros/as somos = We are
Vosotros/as sois = You(all) are (Spain)
Ellos/Ellas/Ustedes son = They/You(all) are

Appearance patterns:
Él es alto. = He is tall.
Ella es baja. = She is short.
Ella es rubia. = She is blonde.
Él es moreno. = He is dark-haired.
Ella es guapa. = She is beautiful.
Ellos son jóvenes. = They are young.
Nosotros somos delgados. = We are thin.

Agreement: Adjectives must agree in gender and number with the subject.
Singular: alto/a, bajo/a, rubio/a, moreno/a, guapo/a, delgado/a
Plural: altos/as, bajos/as, rubios/as, morenos/as, guapos/as, delgados/as

Ella es alta y delgada. = She is tall and thin.
Ellos son altos y morenos. = They are tall and dark-haired.
Ellas son bajas y rubias. = They are short and blonde.

Note: 'Ser' is used for permanent characteristics like height, hair color, and general build. For temporary states (tired, sick), use 'estar' instead.
examples:
Mi madre es alta. (My mother is tall.)
Mi padre es bajo. (My father is short.)
Ella es rubia y guapa. (She is blonde and beautiful.)
Él es moreno y delgado. (He is dark-haired and thin.)
Nosotros somos jóvenes. (We are young.)
Ella es vieja. (She is old.)
Tú eres alto. (You are tall.)
Ellos son delgados. (They are thin.)

La chica es guapa y joven. (The girl is pretty and young.)
El hombre es alto y fuerte. (The man is tall and strong.)
Mi hermana es baja y delgada. (My sister is short and thin.)
El niño es pequeño y rubio. (The boy is small and blonde.)
Las mujeres son altas. (The women are tall.)
Los hombres son bajos. (The men are short.)

grammar.title: Estar + Adjetivo - Describing Temporary States and Wearing Clothes
grammar.content:
The verb ESTAR serves two important functions here:

1) Describing temporary physical states:
Estar cansado/a = to be tired
Estar enfermo/a = to be sick
Estar aburrido/a = to be bored
Estar feliz/triste = to be happy/sad

Ella está cansada. = She is tired.
Nosotros estamos felices. = We are happy.
Él está enfermo. = He is sick.

2) Describing what someone is currently WEARING (estar + vestido/a):
Estar = to be
Vestido/a = dressed/wearing clothes

Ella está vestida. = She is dressed.
Él está vestido de negro. = He is dressed in black.
Ellas están vestidas con un vestido rojo. = They are wearing a red dress.

Combined structure for 'to be wearing':
Estar + vestido/a + con + [clothing item]

Él está vestido con una camisa blanca. = He is wearing a white shirt.
Ella está vestida con un vestido negro. = She is wearing a black dress.
Nosotros estamos vestidos con pantalones y camiseta. = We are wearing pants and a t-shirt.
examples:
Ella está cansada hoy. (She is tired today.)
Nosotros estamos contentos. (We are happy.)
Él está enfermo. (He is sick.)
Ellas están aburridas. (They are bored.)
Ella está vestida con una falda roja. (She is wearing a red skirt.)
Él está vestido con un abrigo marrón. (He is wearing a brown coat.)
Nosotros estamos vestidos con ropa deportiva. (We are wearing sportswear.)
¿Cómo estás vestido hoy? (How are you dressed today?)

grammar.title: Tener + Años - Expressing Age
grammar.content:
In Spanish, age is expressed with the verb TENER (to have), not SER (to be). Literally 'to have X years'.

Conjugation of TENER:
Yo tengo = I have
Tú tienes = You have (informal)
Él/Ella/Usted tiene = He/She/You(formal) has
Nosotros/as tenemos = We have
Vosotros/as tenéis = You(all) have (Spain)
Ellos/Ellas/Ustedes tienen = They/You(all) have

Age expressions:
Tengo 25 años. = I am 25 years old.
Ella tiene 30 años. = She is 30 years old.
¿Cuántos años tienes? = How old are you?
Tú tienes 18 años. = You are 18 years old.
Nosotros tenemos 40 años. = We are 40 years old.
¿Cuántos años tiene él? = How old is he?

Asking about age:
¿Cuántos años tienes? (informal)
¿Cuántos años tiene usted? (formal)
¿Cuántos años tiene? (he/she formal)

Age categories:
Niño/a = child
Joven = young person
Adulto/a = adult
Persona mayor = elderly person

Nota: You cannot use 'ser' for age! 'Él es 25 años' is WRONG. Always use 'tener'.
examples:
Tengo 20 años. (I am 20 years old.)
Ella tiene 25 años. (She is 25 years old.)
Tú tienes 30 años. (You are 30 years old.)
¿Cuántos años tienes? - Tengo 18 años. (How old are you? - I am 18 years old.)
Nosotros tenemos 35 años. (We are 35 years old.)
Él tiene 60 años. (He is 60 years old.)
¿Cuántos años tiene ella? - Tiene 45 años. (How old is she? - She is 45 years old.)
Mi madre tiene 50 años. (My mother is 50 years old.)

grammar.title: Llevar - Wearing / Carrying (Alternative to Estar + Vestido)
grammar.content:
The verb LLEVAR can also express what someone is wearing or carrying.

Conjugation of LLEVAR:
Yo llevo = I wear/carry
Tú llevas = You wear/carry (informal)
Él/Ella/Usted lleva = He/She/You(formal) wears/carries
Nosotros/as llevamos = We wear/carry
Vosotros/as lleváis = You(all) wear/carry (Spain)
Ellos/Ellas/Ustedes llevan = They/You(all) wear/carry

Llevar + clothing item = to be wearing

Yo llevo una camisa blanca. = I am wearing a white shirt.
Tú llevas pantalones negros. = You are wearing black pants.
Ella lleva un vestido rojo. = She is wearing a red dress.
Él lleva una chaqueta azul. = He is wearing a blue jacket.
Nosotros llevamos zapatos marrones. = We are wearing brown shoes.
Ellos llevan sombrero y bufanda. = They are wearing a hat and scarf.

Llevar vs. Estar vestido:
Estar vestido con = more formal way to say 'dressed in'
Llevar + item = more natural, everyday way to say 'wearing'

Llevar also means 'to carry/to take', so context is important.
Ella lleva un bolso grande. = She is carrying a big bag.
Ella lleva un bolso grande = She is wearing a big bag (purse).
examples:
Llevo una camiseta roja. (I am wearing a red t-shirt.)
Llevas una corbata. (You are wearing a tie.)
Ella lleva un vestido largo. (She is wearing a long dress.)
Él lleva unos guantes. (He is wearing gloves.)
Nosotros llevamos botas. (We are wearing boots.)
Llevan una chaqueta y un sombrero. (They are wearing a jacket and a hat.)
¿Qué llevas puesto hoy? (What are you wearing today?)
Llevo los pantalones negros. (I am wearing the black pants.)

grammar.title: Los Artículos y los Sustantivos Plurales - Articles and Plurals
grammar.content:
Spanish nouns have gender (masculine/feminine) and number (singular/plural). This is essential for clothing vocabulary.

Definite articles:
el = the (m. singular)
la = the (f. singular)
los = the (m. plural)
las = the (f. plural)

Indefinite articles:
un = a/an (m. singular)
una = a/an (f. singular)
unos = some (m. plural)
unas = some (f. plural)

Clothing nouns by gender:
Masculine: el pantalón, el abrigo, el suéter, el sombrero, el zapato, el calcetín, el cinturón, el bolso, el pijama, el botón, el cuello, el bolsillo, el chubasquero, el bañador, el bigote, el pecho, el pelo
Feminine: la camisa, la camiseta, la falda, la chaqueta, la bufanda, la gorra, la corbata, la media, la sandalia, la zapatilla, la ropa interior, la chaqueta, la tela, la cremallera, la manga, la talla, la barba, la cara, la cabeza, la frente, la cintura, la rodilla, la nariz, la boca, las orejas

Important: Many clothing items are ALWAYS plural:
los pantalones (pants)
los zapatos (shoes)
las sandalias (sandals)
las botas (boots)
los guantes (gloves)
los calcetines (socks)
las medias (socks/tights)
los pendientes (earrings)
las manos (hands)
las piernas (legs)
los ojos (eyes)
las rodillas (knees)
los brazos (arms)

Plural formation:
Word ending in consonant: add -es
un zapato -> los zapatos
un calcetín -> los calcetines
un bolso -> los bolsos

Word ending in vowel: add -s
la camisa -> las camisas
el botón -> los botones
la falda -> las faldas

Word ending in -z: change to -ces
el lápiz -> los lápices (not clothing but same rule)
examples:
el abrigo -> los abrigos (the coat -> the coats)
la camisa -> las camisas (the shirt -> the shirts)
una falda -> unas faldas (a skirt -> some skirts)
unos guantes -> las botas (some gloves -> the boots)
la ropa interior (underwear - always singular)
los pantalones cortos (shorts - always plural)
la camisa blanca (the white shirt - adjective after noun)
los zapatos negros (the black shoes - adjective after noun)
un vestido rojo (a red dress)
una chaqueta verde (a green jacket)

grammar.title: Adjetivos Demostrativos - This/That Clothing Items
grammar.content:
Demonstrative adjectives point to specific items and must agree in gender and number with the noun they modify.

Near the speaker (this/these):
este/esta = this (m/f singular)
estos/estas = these (m/f plural)

Medium distance (that/those):
eso -> ese/esa = that (m/f singular)
esos/esas = those (m/f plural)

Far from both (that over there/those over there):
aquel/aquella = that over there (m/f singular)
aquellos/aquellas = those over there (m/f plural)

With clothing:
Esta camisa es roja. = This shirt is red.
Estos pantalones son negros. = These pants are black.
Ese vestido es bonito. = That dress is pretty.
Esas botas son nuevas. = Those boots are new.
Este abrigo es muy caro. = This coat is very expensive.
Esa falda es larga. = That skirt is long.

Nota: In everyday Spanish, 'ese/esa' is often used for both 'that' and 'this' depending on context. The 'aquel' forms are less common.

Demonstrative pronouns (without the noun):
Este = this one (m.)
Esa = that one (f.)
Estos = these ones (m. pl.)
Esas = those ones (f. pl.)

¿Quieres este vestido? - Sí, quiero ese. (Do you want this dress? - Yes, I want that one.)
¿De quién son estos zapatos? - Son míos. (Whose shoes are these? - They are mine.)
examples:
Esta falda es nueva. (This skirt is new.)
Ese sombrero es viejo. (That hat is old.)
Estas sandalias son grandes. (These sandals are big.)
Esas gafas son bonitas. (Those glasses are pretty.)
Este zapato no me queda. (This shoe doesn't fit me.)
¿Te gusta esa camisa? - Sí, me gusta esa camisa. (Do you like that shirt? - Yes, I like that shirt.)
Quiero estos guantes. (I want these gloves.)
¿Cuánto cuesta esa chaqueta? (How much is that jacket?)

exercises.question: Complete: 'Él tiene ___ años.' (He is 30 years old.)
exercises.explanation: 'Treinta' = 30. 'Él tiene treinta años.'

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ella es ___ y ___.' (She is blonde and beautiful.)
exercises.explanation: Both adjectives must agree with 'ella' (feminine): 'rubia' and 'guapa'. 'Ella es rubia y guapa.'

exercises.question: Complete: '___ guantes son nuevos.' (These gloves are new.)
exercises.explanation: 'Guantes' is masculine plural, so use 'Estos'. 'Estos guantes son nuevos.'

exercises.question: Complete: '¿Cuántos ___ tienes?' (How old are you?)
exercises.explanation: '¿Cuántos años tienes?' = How old are you? Literally: 'How many years do you have?'

exercises.question: Complete: '___ camisa es azul.' (This shirt is blue.)
exercises.explanation: 'Camisa' is feminine singular, so use 'Esta'. 'Esta camisa es azul.'

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'She is wearing a dress'?
exercises.explanation: 'Llevar' is used for what someone is wearing. 'Ella lleva un vestido.' 'Ser' (es) cannot be used with clothing items.

exercises.question: Which clothing item is always plural in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Los pantalones' is always plural (like in English). 'El abrigo', 'la camisa', and 'el sombrero' are singular.

exercises.question: What does 'guapo/a' mean in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Guapo/a' = handsome (m.) / beautiful (f.). 'Alto/a' = tall. 'Delgado/a' = thin. 'Viejo/a' = old.

exercises.question: What is 'eyebrows' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Las cejas' = eyebrows. 'Los ojos' = eyes. 'Las pestañas' = eyelashes. 'La nariz' = nose.

exercises.question: What is 'eyelashes' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Las pestañas' = eyelashes. 'Las cejas' = eyebrows. 'Los ojos' = eyes. 'La frente' = forehead.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Yo ___ una chaqueta negra.' (I am wearing a black jacket.)
exercises.explanation: 'Llevar' is used for wearing clothes. 'Yo llevo una chaqueta negra.'

exercises.question: What is 'the shoes' (plural article + shoes)?
exercises.explanation: 'Zapatos' is masculine plural. Los + zapatos = los zapatos.

exercises.question: What is 'the skirt'?
exercises.explanation: 'Falda' is feminine singular. La + falda = la falda.
